messages:
Sam: PagerDuty alert: PD-8910 for service `model-serving` triggered — sudden increase in 500s from hosted API and latency spikes. Paging oncall. https://pagerduty.example/PD-8910 :rotating_light:
PagerDuty: PagerDuty notification: Incident PD-8910 \u2014 model-serving. Trigger: 5xx rate > 4% for 2m. Urgency: high. Paging primary: Sam. Escalation policy: primary->secondary(Zoe)->manager(Claire).
Sam: ack PD-8910. I'm checking recent deploys and looking at autoscaler.
Sam: quick note: deploys show no config change in last 24h. Metrics dashboard: pod queue depth jumped, memory pressure visible on several GPUs.
Zoe: I just got the PD escalation but my phone was on DND (missed the first call). Picking up now.
IncidentBot: Escalation: secondary (Zoe) notified at 21:12:58 UTC.
PagerDuty: PagerDuty escalation: Manager Claire notified (no ack from secondary within timeout).
Claire: Claire here, I'm awake. What's the damage?
Sam: errors ~4.8% peaked, some 5xx are CUDA OOMs. No immediate customer data-loss reports. Trying to scale cluster; autoscaler isn't reacting due to maxReplicas=8.
Miguel: oncall infra — can temporarily bump replica cap. I'll SSH to cluster to validate and snapshot heap.
Miguel: paste of recent logs:
```
W0422 21:10:05.441 model-runner[pid=3321] KV cache miss=1.2e6, queue_len=312
E0422 21:10:07.782 model-runner[pid=3321] RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating tensor of size 1024
```
Zoe: since my mobile missed, PD escalation path worked. I'll help coordinate scaling and route failover. Suggest flipping traffic to the standby lighter-quant model in the EU region for non-low-latency customers.
Sam: agree. Miguel — can you raise maxReplicas to 20 for the `serve-realtime` HPA? Command I ran locally (dry): `kubectl patch hpa serve-realtime -n inference -p '{"spec": {"maxReplicas": 20}}'`
Miguel: applying patch now. Also creating temporary escape hatch: set `SERVE_MODEL_VARIANT=small-quant` on the ingress routing rule for 20% of traffic.
IncidentBot: Command executed by Miguel: `kubectl patch hpa serve-realtime -n inference` 1:13:12 UTC.
PagerDuty: PD-8910: acknowledged by Sam. Manager Claire on-call.
Zoe: doing rolling update to enable prefix KV caching and reduce memory per request. `kubectl set env deploy/model-runner PREFIX_CACHE=enabled -n inference`
Sam: routing change applied for 20% traffic -> small-quant variant. Observability: error rate starting to drop; tail latency smaller for routed traffic.
Miguel: HPA maxReplicas increased to 20. New pods coming up in ~60s. Queue depth 300 -> 90 now.
Claire: thanks. Any customers affected that we should proactively notify?
Sam: support sync: expected impact window ~21:09-21:16 UTC. We should notify customers with SLO-sensitive tiers — estimate ~2.7% of requests in window returned 5xx, mostly transient. No lost payloads.
Zoe: confirm no failed webhooks or persistent job failures; retried requests went through.
Miguel: note: autoscaler config needs review: scale-up stabilization and maxReplicas too conservative for bursty traffic.
IncidentBot: Ticket created: https://tickets.example/ENG-9001 "review HPA limits and default model cache policy" by Miguel.
Sam: adding runbook action: alert when queue_len & mem_pressure coincide for >30s. Create followup task to add synthetic load test.
Claire: Manager note: PD escalation path worked as intended (secondary missed initial mobile alert). Please include mobile timeout config and oncall DND guidance in postmortem.
PagerDuty: PD-8910 status: monitoring  acknowledged, mitigation applied (traffic split + HPA bump + cache enable).
Sam: monitoring for 45m then handoff. Planning to draft postmortem with timeline and RCA items.
Miguel: will revert emergency traffic split after stabilization and propose a staged rollout for small-quant variant.
Zoe: mobile timeout adjusted during incident (reduced from 5m to 1m for secondary) so future escalations happen faster.
Sam: final quick impact summary for notes: peak error rate 4.8% between 21:09-21:14 UTC; affected customers experienced increased latency and retryable 500s; no evidence of data loss; root causes: HPA maxReplicas too low for burst, prefix cache disabled by default, memory pressure causing OOMs.
Claire: good work. Please file all follow-ups under ENG-9001 and schedule oncall/handoff review. I'll close PD when we're comfortable.
IncidentBot: Incident PD-8910 updated to "monitoring".
Sam: handing off monitoring to Zoe at 22:00 UTC. Zoe: please escalate immediately if any regression. :thumbsup:
